newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Senior Vietnam official seeks news overhaul.
newsitem.headline: Senior Vietnam official seeks news overhaul.

text.p: A senior member of Vietnam's politburo has called for an overhaul of the state-run Vietnam News Agency to promote its role as the premier source of official information about Vietnam.

Lieutenant-general Le Kha Phieu told VNA officials at a meeting last month that Hanoi could not monopolize information in Vietnam but should seek to manage news to compete with unsanctioned information from foreign news organisations.
"From hunting for news to reporting stories, we should be first, and cannot be behind," he said. A text of the speech carried on Saturday by the Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper.
"We should not allow any foreign newspapers or news agencies to usurp...the official voice of the Party and State."
Phieu, who ranks fifth on the politburo and occupies a position on the elite inner standing board, said VNA should not underestimate the power of information.

"Whether you are called a news agency or something else, the Vietnam News Agency is still a very important political tool of our party and state," he said. "Your information must imply political orientation."
Government officials, apparently concerned about critical foreign news reports, in recent months have called for improvements to domestic news organisations as a way to tackle the problem.
Measures have also been taken to rein in foreign news organisations and journalists, including a restrictive foreign press law that took effect earlier this month.
